english:
We offer millions upon millions of thanks to Jesus and the Blessed Mother for allowing us to set foot on the holy soil of the Blessed Mother.
My name is Honey. I come from Taliparamba in Kannur district. This is my daughter Diya. I came here through my husband’s family.
The reason we took this covenant is that from a young age, when my daughter was studying in fifth standard, she always had headaches and dizziness.
The teachers from her school would call me frequently. When we showed her to doctors, they said there was no problem.
When an eye doctor came to the school and tested her, they said that one eye had poor vision.
Then we took her to another hospital, and the doctor there said that she was using only one eye.
The other eye was not being used. Because of that, the doctor said that 99% of the vision in that eye was lost. We became very tense.
Then we came here and took the covenant. After coming here, praying, and attending Holy Mass, my daughter told me that she felt a speck go into her eye.
She asked me, “Mother, please blow on my eye once.” I gently blew on her eye. Then suddenly she started crying a lot.
I told her not to cry and asked her to pray to the Mother. I told her that the Mother would give her sight again.
Then she told me that she could clearly see Jesus and the Blessed Mother.
But when we showed her to the doctors, they said that the child had lost 99% of vision in that eye.
Since she was very young, they said exercises could not be given for that eye. They said she was using only the other eye.
Therefore, they said she could see only with one eye. But as a result of coming here and praying, now my daughter can clearly see all of us.
After this, she received a very good testimony. She herself will say it. About my prayer life—earlier I was not someone who prayed regularly every day.
But now, as a result of taking this covenant, I make the sign of the Cross every day, I read the Bible for half an hour,
and in whatever way I can, I help those who ask me for help.
And the experience my daughter had—my daughter herself will tell it.
My name is Diya. I am studying in seventh standard. I thank the Blessed Mother and Jesus.
When I was studying in sixth standard, I had an exam.
It was Sanskrit and Hindi.
All those days, my mother was the one who used to teach me. One day, when my mother went out, I was alone.
Only my younger brother and I were at home. Because of the noise he was making while playing, I couldn’t study, so I sent him outside.
I sent him out and closed the door. I couldn’t understand anything, and I wasn’t able to study at all.
Then I went near the mother's statue, knelt down, and prayed to the Blessed Mother. I said, “I can’t study. I’m not able to read.
It is very tough. Mother, please help me. I am not able to study at all. Please give me the wisdom to study.” I knelt down and prayed, crying.
Then I went into the room. When I looked at the place where I had been praying,
I saw something like a small gust of fire falling down. I ran towards it, and at that moment, I saw the Blessed Mother standing there.
Then I knelt down there. The Blessed Mother touched my head and blessed me. My entire head was under the Blessed Mother’s hand.
I felt an intense cold. My hands and legs were trembling and had become very cold. At that moment, I ran outside, and by then, the Blessed Mother had disappeared.
I quickly opened the door and told my younger brother. He became very frightened, and then I called my mother. My mother came.
When my mother came, she asked me everything in detail. The Mother I saw was not like the statue that is kept here.
She looks like this but the dress was not this color. It was a color like rose and white.
After I explained everything and my mother understood, in that exam I got very good marks—25 and 24 out of 25
Those were the marks I got in both Sanskrit and Hindi. I thank the Blessed Mother and Jesus.
From the Gospel of Matthew, chapter 20, verses 30 to 34: "When two blind men sitting by the roadside heard that Jesus was passing by,
they cried out loudly, “Lord, Son of David, have mercy on us.” Jesus stopped,
called them, and asked, “What do you want me to do for you?” They replied, “Lord, we want our eyes to be opened.” Moved with compassion,
Jesus touched their eyes. Immediately they received their sight, and they followed Him."
Dear brothers and sisters, Honey here first shared at this altar the testimony about the eyesight her child received.
Nearly 99 percent of the vision in one eye was lost, and the child was seeing everything only with one eye.
Even with treatment, the doctors said that regaining the vision would be very difficult. In such a situation, the mother and daughter came here to the holy presence of the Mother of Kreupasanam,
took the covenant, offered the child’s intention, and prayed.
Realizing that receiving sight was extremely difficult, the mother entrusted this great intention into the hands of the Blessed Mother.
By using the covenant items and continuously participating in the covenant meditation of the Father fully surrendering to the Mother,
the vision of that eye was restored, and the doctors themselves certified that the eyesight had returned.
Beloved ones, even today the power of God is at work. Even today, God continues to give reminders and experiences—through signs and encounters, saying, “I am with you,” to those who live surrendered to God.
The child also specifically testified about the vision she received—seeing the Blessed Mother in person, and the moments when the Blessed Mother touched her, embraced her, and blessed her.
We read in the Word that elders will see dreams, children will receive visions, and young men and women will prophesy. The Word never tells us things that do not happen.
At all times, when the working of the Spirit of God flows into us—beyond human thoughts, beyond logic, and beyond the ordinary activities of daily life—the presence of God leads us into great things.
Through the covenant, the Blessed Mother comes in search of her children, and by filling those who surrender to her with the Holy Spirit, she sets their lives in order.
That is why the entire first part of the covenant is focused on removing whatever stands as an obstacle to our spiritual life,
whatever hinders a divine relationship and a divine dialogue—those sinful states, unhealthy relationships, attachments, and addictions— so that they may be removed from us.
That is why, at the beginning, we write down and submit the person or things that we firmly believe should leave our lives.
From the moment we write and submit this, if we are faithful to God, we begin to recognize the stains and shortcomings in our lives,
and with an open heart we are able to confess them before God, desiring that they be purified.
When we surrender these weaknesses and sinful stains before God with such longing,
we can see that Jesus grants us the spiritual strength to turn away from those weaknesses and sins.
Just as we decide what we must renounce and distance ourselves from in life, in the same way we also write what we desire on the other side—these are the "intentions".
According to the covenant, we must remember that it is not enough for our intentions alone to be sincere;
our decision before God to let go of what must leave our lives must also be sincere,
because God sees both the inside and the outside equally. Nothing is hidden from His eyes.
Therefore, there is no obligation that we must be blessed simply because we do a little prayer, a little charity, and a little sharing of God’s Word.
Because the Lord knows very well what we were yesterday, how we live today, and how we will behave tomorrow if we receive a blessing.
Therefore, when we prepare ourselves to offer a life of clarity, humility, and holiness before God,
God stands with us, blesses our way of life with the special protection of the Blessed Mother, and accepts our intentions.
Therefore, let us pray in His presence for a life that is acceptable to God.
Giving thanks to the Blessed Mother and the Holy Son for every blessing and spiritual grace received in this family, let us offer this testimony with applause.
